_comment: The mechanical rules are regexes run in code. The criteria are what needs judgement and go to the model. Keep the split: never ask a model to find an em dash.

mechanical.message: the 'not just X, it's Y' construction

mechanical.pattern: \b(it's worth noting|needless to say|that being said|in conclusion|at the end of the day)\b

mechanical.message: 'helps you' construction instead of a direct statement

mechanical.pattern: \b(experts agree|studies show|research shows|industry reports indicate|users love|customers enjoy)\b
\b(streamline workflows?|drive innovation|unlock value|maximi[sz]e efficiency|scale with confidence|digital transformation|built (with|for) the future|designed for the future|in mind)\b
^\s*(Certainly|Absolutely|Great question|Of course)[!,]|\bin today's fast[- ]paced\b|\bin the ever[- ]evolving\b|\bin the realm of\b

criteria.rule: Every claim carries a number, a name, a timeline or an example. A sentence that could appear on 500 other sites scores low.
It is clear who this is for and what changes for them after using it.
The most important information is first. No closing paragraph that restates the section.
Sentence length varies. A page where every sentence has the same shape scores low even if each one is fine.
No claim the draft cannot support: invented statistics, unnamed sources, opinions attributed to users.
